480	It became a byword, and a thorn in the eyes of everyone who hates Torah
481	in Israel and around the world.
482	But the Sephardic picture is still missing.
483	And the truth is that the fall of the Sephardim was infinitely greater than the fall of
484	the Ashkenazim upon arriving in Eretz Israel.
485	If the Shoah struck and cut down the Ashkenazi Torah world,
486	then the Zionists, the Erev Rav, the leftists, the Mapainiks, call them
487	whatever names you like, damaged the Sephardic Torah world. The problem:
488	Before they came to Eretz Israel, there was not one Sephardi from the Eastern communities
489	or Yemen who desecrated Shabbat. There was no such thing. There was no such thing. But
490	deliberate, targeted actions were carried out by the immigrants
491	here, all kinds of Bolsheviks who came up from Russia, haters of
492	religion, who wanted to set the tone and turn everyone who came here into a secular person like them.
493	Anyone who knew what the communities of Yemen, Djerba, Baghdad were like, even though the Alliance
494	had already entered a little, still you had no open Shabbat desecrator who came here to Eretz Israel.
495	Only once they arrived in the land, actions were taken to uproot religion from them,
496	from the Sephardim.
497	This is simple and clear.
498	The Rav of Brisk once said: why did they establish a state?
499	To uproot religion from the people.
500	Let's see you cut peyot in Yemen, if the Yemenite police didn't come after you.
501	Let's see you try to sabotage Torah study in Baghdad, if the Iraqi
502	police didn't come after you. But when you brought everyone up here to Eretz Israel and you set the tone, then
503	no one tells you what to do or how to act. So what happened, gentlemen? They tried
504	to uproot Torah entirely from the Eastern communities and the Yemenites, by force
505	and with brutality, with threats that they would get no food if they ran off to the religious. On food,
506	they would starve them if they wanted to keep Torah and mitzvot. They made girls and boys dance, away
507	from their parents, with terrible immodesty. They take a chicken, close the door, bang the
508	chicken against the door and eat it. On Shabbat they go
509	to the orchards, pick fruit: "See, nothing happened to me, what do you want?"
510	Mass Shabbat desecration. They threatened that they would not get work, and that a school would not
511	get budgets if Torah and mitzvot were taught there.
512	They deliberately interfered with their Torah studies.
513	And now you'll say, you're being fed by all kinds of preachers, demagogues of every sort.
514	No, gentlemen, everything I am telling you now is not even a fraction of what a government
515	commission of inquiry established, everything I am saying now.
516	This was in 1950, January 1950, that a governmental
517	commission of inquiry was established, called the Frumkin Commission.
518	There was a judge, called Gad Frumkin, and he was authorized by the commission to go
519	and examine the immigrants' claims of secular coercion.
520	Of secular coercion.
521	A government commission.
522	It is not that today you are investigating what happened 50 years or 70 years ago.
523	You are investigating, speaking of January 1950. When was the state founded? In '48.
524	You are talking here about two years after, two or three years after the founding of the state.
525	That is, the events were fresh.
526	They received dozens of testimonies that they were interfered with, their peyot were cut off,
527	they said as if shorn.
528	They cut off their peyot, forced them to desecrate Shabbat.
529	There was enormous pressure on Ben-Gurion and Zalman Shazar and their friends, who tried to sabotage
530	the commission and its results. It did not help them. The commission
531	was published as an official government report, after collecting dozens of testimonies, that all these claims
532	were true claims. There was here, beyond any doubt, a drive to turn everyone secular and to uproot
533	their religion. It was all in the circles of the Histadrut, under Nachum Levin, who, following
534	the report, was removed from his post.
535	There is a saying in Latin. I took this sentence from the report; I read the entire report
536	to prepare this lesson for you.
537	It is written there that there is a sentence in Latin that says: whoever holds the government
538	determines the religion of the people.
539	So now, since the leftists were the ones who came here
540	at first, they determined the religion of the people and uprooted Torah from them,
541	and forced on them what Stalin did not force; they completed the job.
542	Why?
543	They could not tolerate the religious, Jewish, Diaspora, traditional markers.
544	They did not want Jews; they wanted blind men, they wanted...
545	a pioneering, renewing, modern, secular state.
546	They could not tolerate any of the religious, traditional, Diaspora markers.
547	And to our great sorrow, even the Ashkenazi religious were alienated from the Sephardic religious.
548	And so the Mapai people sensed that the weak chain could be broken.
549	Who was the weak one?
550	The Sephardim.
551	And so whom did they go after?
552	The Sephardim and the Yemenites,
553	the Moroccans and the Djerbans. To cut them off, they moved some of the children to secular educational
554	institutions, to boarding schools, to secular kibbutzim. They told them, "Your father is old-fashioned, your mother is
555	old-fashioned, now the counselor will teach you." And so it was. They laughed and mocked anyone who kept
556	Torah. One of the biggest scandals in this country is the abduction of the Yemenite children.
557	I tell you, people: they put their child, they took him: "Your child is sick," they told them, "he is
558	sick."
559	They took him. I am talking about thousands of babies.
560	Thousands of babies and children, not hundreds.
561	Thousands of babies.
562	They told them, "Your child is sick, your son, we will take him to the hospital."
563	After two days the parents come to the hospital to visit the child, and they were told, "He died."
564	What?
565	Where is the body?
566	"We buried him."
567	"Here," they lift some earth for them, "here he is buried."
568	Do you know what they did here?
569	Do you know what failures there were in this country when it was founded?
570	And what did they do with the... they took them to all kinds of kibbutzim, made them completely secular, and the most striking part:
571	when their draft time came, suddenly they receive a draft order at home.
572	And then the parents understood: "Wow, how did a draft order come to the house?
573	Why does it not say in the offices that he died?
574	Apparently he did not die."
575	Do you know what went on here?
576	Come on, I have no time to get into these links, but understand how targeted the drive was to uproot religion.
577	There was a lot of naivety, what can I tell you?
578	They believed in simplicity that the State of Israel was the beginning of the redemption; the great sages of the generation slept with
579	the JNF collection box.
580	Do you know what the Jewish National Fund box is?
581	Asleep.
582	I still remember that when we were little, in school they would put this
583	box in front of us. Do you remember the Jewish National Fund box?
584	A dunam here and a dunam there, clod after clod, Miri Regev.
585	What do you want?
586	They believed.
587	You know, now, from whom did they buy clod after clod?
588	From the Turks, from the Ottomans who ruled here.
589	For years the JNF did not sell land to Muslims.
590	Because when I put in money, I put it in to redeem the land of the nation, meaning the people of Israel.
591	There was a High Court petition about this: a Muslim petitioned, asking why the JNF doesn't sell to us.
592	The High Court said he was right, and they began selling to them too.
593	Do you understand what happened?
594	And this is money that I put in the box to redeem the nation's land, to buy it from the Turks, and in the end they sell it
595	to Muslims. So what did we gain by this?
596	What did the sages accomplish with their decree?
597	They arrived in Morocco, gentlemen, and told the people in Morocco: we will bring your children
598	first, and afterward the elders. There is no time to bring the elders. They came to the parents
599	and said: which yeshiva do you want, shall we take your children?
